Q: Need assistance with regular expression format A:

If you wanted to make it a world class ant-duplication you could run two different regex on it.

First remove repetition between groups of dissimilar characters. -

([^a-zA-Z0-9\r\n]+)\1+ https://regex101.com/r/i04Lfi/1/substitution

Second remove the repetition between identical characters -

([^a-zA-Z0-9\r\n])\1+ https://regex101.com/r/i04Lfi/2/substitution

In both cases replace by $1

Q: What programming tasks do you still prefer to do without AI? A:

Computer vision engineer here. My work is mostly python and c++.

I use claude code to help me write one off scripts that I can easily check the output of, for example, when making plots, etc. I've also had some luck using it to make little web dashboards to track things, basically internal tools for the company I work at.

I've found empirically that if I use it on production code, I end up having to rewrite it because there's subtle assumptions or mistakes in the code that don't surface until later, and I don't build a good mental model of what the code is doing in my head. Hence I mostly end up just using the web based UI to look up syntax stuff when I'm programming.

I also like to take "breaks" from even the webUI where I just code traditional style with stack overflow and docs open to keep myself from getting lazy.

Q: What comes after the %? A:

10.1f means floating point with 10 characters wide with one place after the decimal point. If the number has less than 10 digits, it's padded with spaces. 10.2f is the same, but with two places after the decimal point.

You have these basic types:

%d   - integer
%x   - hex integer
%s   - string
%c   - char (only one)
%f   - floating point (float)
%d   - signed int (decimal)
%i   - signed int (integer) (same as decimal).
%u   - unsigned int
%ld  - long (signed) int
%lu  - long unsigned int
%lld - long long (signed) int
%llu - long long unsigned int

There are several others listed in @Eli's response (man 3 printf).

Q: Netflix catalogue by country A:

Ended up here looking for the same thing. I'm a bit late to the party but, for future readers, there now are a few APIs providing up-to-date country-based catalogs, and not just for Netflix.

See the Movie of the Night Streaming Availability API and the JustWatch Streaming API.
